title: Pulse mode division-by-zero at high frequencies
description: 500'000 / outputFreqHz yields 0 when outputFreqHz >= 500001 (commands '6'=1MHz, '7'=10MHz). pulseHalfPeriodUs=0 causes loopPulse() to toggle every iteration (uncontrolled) and triggerImpulse() to call delayMicroseconds(0). Fix: clamp outputFreqHz to max 500kHz for pulse mode, or guard the division.

title: Hex format width too narrow for >16 output pins
description: In main.cpp:174, Serial.printf uses %04lX format (4 hex digits = 16 bits max). The safety check allows up to 20 output pins, meaning input values can reach 0xFFFFF (5 hex digits). The format string should use at least %05lX or %06lX, or dynamically compute the hex width based on numOutputs to handle the full allowed range.
close_reason: Fixed in b0ddd9a: input hex format widened to %05lX (up to 20 pins = 0xFFFFF)

title: Serial newline characters trigger printHeader() unexpectedly
description: In main.cpp:278, the serial command handler triggers printHeader() on \r and \n in addition to 'p'/'P'. This means opening a serial terminal (which often sends a newline) or pressing Enter floods the console with the truth table header. Remove \r and \n from the condition so only 'p'/'P' triggers the config dump.
close_reason: Fixed in 4bb2087: only 'p'/'P' triggers printHeader(), \r/\n removed from condition

title: LEDC base clock hardcoded to 40 MHz — wrong for ESP32-S3
description: maxLedcResolution() uses hardcoded 40MHz but ESP32-S3 APB clock is 80MHz. This underestimates available resolution on S3, resulting in coarser PWM than necessary. Should detect actual APB clock or use a per-target constant.

title: Verify BUILTIN_LED_PIN defined for ESP32-S3 env
description: The code uses #error if BUILTIN_LED_PIN is not defined. The new [env:function-generator-esp32s3] extends hw:default-esp32s3 — need to verify that section defines BUILTIN_LED_PIN, otherwise the build will fail.
close_reason: Verified: hw:seeed-xiao-esp32s3-plus defines -DBUILTIN_LED_PIN=21; function-generator-esp32s3 env inherits it and builds

title: writeGPIOAB() clobbers all 16 pins including input pin OLAT state
description: In main.cpp:127-128, writeGPIOAB() writes all 16 pins at once on each MCP. For pins configured as INPUT, this sets their OLAT register to 0. Currently benign since inputs have no pull-ups, but fragile — if pull-ups are ever enabled on input pins, the OLAT write could interact unexpectedly. Either document this deliberate choice or use a read-modify-write approach that only touches output pin bits.
close_reason: Deliberate choice documented in code (main.cpp:216): inputs are Hi-Z, OLAT write is benign

title: Introduce ROLE_CLK pin role with dedicated clock handling for registered PAL outputs
description:
Currently CLK is mapped as a regular ROLE_OUTPUT pin (bit 0 of the input counter). While the LSB naturally toggles every step, this doesn't properly handle registered PAL outputs that latch on clock edges.

Introduce a dedicated ROLE_CLK pin role that is not treated as a regular PAL input:

**Requirements:**
1. **ROLE_CLK pin role** — distinct from ROLE_OUTPUT; excluded from the input combination counter
2. **Clock toggling before reads** — CLK must be explicitly toggled (not just part of the counter) before reading outputs
3. **Dual-edge support** — support both rising-edge and falling-edge clocking (some PALs register on fall)
4. **Clocked vs clockless modes** — distinguish:
   - **Clockless (combinational):** no ROLE_CLK pins configured; current brute-force enumeration works as-is
   - **Clocked (registered):** ROLE_CLK pin(s) present; for each input combination, explicitly toggle CLK and read after the active edge

**Current behavior (bit 0 as CLK):**
- Counter increments: 0→1→2→3→...
- CLK (bit 0) toggles: L→H→L→H→...
- Outputs are read after each step, but there's no explicit clock cycle per input combination

**Desired behavior (ROLE_CLK):**
- Counter enumerates only non-CLK output pins
- For each combination: set outputs → toggle CLK (low→high or high→low depending on edge config) → settling delay → read outputs
- Truth table rows represent: inputs → outputs (after clock edge)
close_reason: Implemented ROLE_CLK pin role in cf10f78. Clock pin is excluded from the input counter and toggled explicitly (low→high) per combination. No mode switch — if ROLE_CLK present, clock cycles; if absent, pure combinational. ATF22V10C config updated to use ROLE_CLK for pin 0.

title: README: update stale Status section
description: The Status section still says 'initializes both MCP23017s and reads/dumps raw GPIO state. Pin role configuration, input enumeration, and truth table output are not yet implemented.' All of that is now implemented. Update to reflect current state.
close_reason: Updated Status section to reflect implemented functionality

title: README: fix input count and row count in example output
description: README says '13 inputs (CLK + 12 data)' and '2^13 = 8192 rows' but the code has 12 outputs (driving 12 PAL inputs), producing 2^12 = 4096 rows. Update to match.
close_reason: Fixed: 13→12 inputs, 8192→4096 rows in README example output section

title: Frequency commands misleading in cosine mode
description: Pressing '0'-'7' while in cosine mode prints '→ Frequency: N Hz' but the DAC cosine output stays fixed at 1kHz. Either suppress the frequency change in cosine mode, or note in the serial output that cosine frequency is unchanged.

title: Rename setSquareFreq to match shared outputFreqHz usage
description: setSquareFreq() modifies outputFreqHz (shared across all modes) but has a square-specific name. Consider renaming to applyOutputFreq or inlining into setFreq for clarity.
close_reason: Fixed in 3381731: setSquareFreq renamed to applyOutputFreq

title: Help text says 0-6 but code handles 0-7
description: printHelp() shows '0-6 - Set frequency to 10^N Hz' but the switch statement handles '0' through '7'. Either update the help text to 0-7 or remove the '7' case.
close_reason: Help text updated to '0-7 - Set frequency to 10^N Hz', matching the 0-7 switch cases

title: No way to reconfigure pins without reset when swapping PAL chips
description: Once setup() runs, pin roles are fixed from the compiled pinRoles array. If a user swaps the PAL chip under test for one with different pin assignments, there's no way to reconfigure without a full reset/reflash. Consider adding a serial command to reinitialize pin configuration, or document that a reset is required when changing chips.

title: No lib_deps declared for Adafruit_MCP23X17 in platformio.ini
description: The mcp23017-pal-tester env sections in platformio.ini don't declare lib_deps for Adafruit_MCP23X17. The code works because the library is manually installed in lib/, which is consistent with other envs in the project. However, this is a portability issue — cloning the repo fresh won't auto-install the dependency. Consider adding lib_deps for better PlatformIO best practices.

title: Clarify output/input terminology in printHeader()
description: printHeader() says 'Outputs: N, Inputs: N' referring to MCP pin directions, but this is confusing because MCP outputs drive PAL inputs and vice versa. Consider labelling as 'PAL inputs' / 'PAL outputs' or 'drive pins' / 'read pins' to avoid ambiguity.
close_reason: Relabelled all user-facing output to use PAL perspective: 'PAL inputs'/'PAL outputs' instead of MCP-centric 'Outputs'/'Inputs'

title: Remove unused testRunning flag
description: testRunning is set/cleared in runTest() but never checked anywhere. Either remove it or use it to support an abort mechanism via serial interrupt.

title: Remove unused mask variables in buildPinMaps()
description: mcp0OutputMask, mcp0InputMask, mcp1OutputMask, mcp1InputMask are computed in buildPinMaps() but never read anywhere. Either remove them or use them for optimized masked writes in writeOutputs()/readInputs().
close_reason: Removed 4 unused mask variables and their computation in buildPinMaps()

title: Whitespace normalization mixed into feature commit
description: The commit 0845e87 normalizes indentation from inconsistent spacing to 4-space indentation in the mpu6050-demo and function-generator platformio.ini sections. This is a good cleanup but mixed into the mcp23017-pal-tester feature commit, making the diff noisier. Ideally whitespace-only changes should be in a separate commit.
close_reason: Fixed - whitespace normalization separated from feature commit

title: LED polarity is inverted on Wemos D1 Mini but not documented
description: The built-in LED on Wemos D1 Mini is active-low (HIGH=off, LOW=on). The code uses HIGH in setup (LED off) and LOW in error blink (LED on briefly), which is functionally correct. However, the inverted logic isn't documented in comments. The ESP32-S3 variant uses OUTPUT_OPEN_DRAIN which has different behavior. Add a comment clarifying the LED polarity assumptions.
close_reason: Fixed in a6a2940: LED polarity documented for D1 Mini (active-low) and ESP32/S3 (open-drain)

title: Fix double-tab indentation in platformio.ini for mcp23017-pal-tester
description: The mcp23017-pal-tester env uses double tabs for build_src_filter indentation while every other env in the file uses single tabs. Normalize to single tabs.
close_reason: Normalized double tabs to single tabs in mcp23017-pal-tester build_src_filter
